turn.context: Four roles, two sizing chains: the admissions side settled on the hospital’s numbers, the discharge side waiting for its discharge pattern. Full cost, not extra cost, said plainly.

transcript.label: Transcript turn 28 · Part 4: Teams and numbers, both sides

text: Four roles. Two managers, and two teams under them.
bullets: The admissions side we can settle. About 41 admissions a day, 5 an hour per person, over a short window. That gives 3 on the afternoon shift.
The discharge side we cannot settle yet. The usual rule of one person for 15 discharges a day gives 3. At another hospital the real answer was 2.
The cost shown is the full cost of these roles, not the extra cost. Send us four numbers and it becomes a difference.
chat.pointer: Pick a role to open it. Move the slider to see how the busiest hour sets the number of staff. Type in any number you have.
chat.invite: Shall we finish with part 5, the measures?
chat.note: The busiest hour sets the number, not the daily average.

sheets.title: Bed Manager
sheets.text: Owns the whole bed plan as one person. The role is about coordination, so it is not sized per admission.
